title: Linux setup lock: replace the non-darwin O_EXCL fallback with kernel-arbitrated locking (WCLI-20 review; prerequisite of WCLI-21)
description: src/adapters/setup-session.ts returns undefined from acquireFlock off darwin, so setup falls to an O_EXCL file with dead-pid reaping (clearStaleLock). The WCLI-20 review measured a check-then-delete race in that fallback: 12 overlapping holder pairs in 20 rounds, with process.platform faked. It is unreachable today only because the key provider refuses non-darwin (src/adapters/keychain.ts). WCLI-21 makes it reachable, so it must be replaced before any Linux key provider lands. The WCLI-20 note is recorded on WCLI-21 (grooming and review notes). Cleared by the leader on 2026-11-08 as the first slice of WCLI-21, independent of the TPM design questions.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On Linux the setup session lock is arbitrated by the kernel through bun:ffi on libc, with no new dependency, and the O_EXCL and dead-pid-reaping fallback is no longer used on Linux

A race test runs real overlapping holders, in separate processes and without faking process.platform, against the real lock and shows at most one holder at a time over many rounds, the rounds on which the old fallback overlapped
The race test runs where Linux semantics are real (the self-hosted Linux CI job), and the task says plainly which environments cannot run it
Any ADR amendment records this locking mechanism only, not the TPM design

implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTATION 2026-11-08 (branch fix/WCLI-152-linux-setup-lock). acquireFlock now takes flock(2) through libc on darwin (libSystem) and linux (libc.so.6); the O_EXCL file, clearStaleLock, lockPid and compare-and-delete release are removed; any other platform, or a missing C library, fails closed (vault_key_store_unsupported / vault_store_failed). I used flock(2), the same call macOS already uses, not fcntl F_SETLK: flock is non-variadic and per open file description, while POSIX F_SETLK locks are per process and drop when any descriptor to the file closes, which would let two holders in one process both succeed. WHERE IT RUNS: the dev machine is macOS, so locally the race test ran only the darwin path (and a mutation that makes the lock a no-op failed it, as predicted). The Linux path is exercised by the self-hosted Linux ARM64 CI job, which is a real Linux kernel; I have not run it anywhere else and ran nothing on jetson. Race test: test/setup.test.ts "the setup lock excludes real overlapping holders" spawns 4 real processes x 150 rounds against the real lock with a no-lock control that must show overlaps; fixtures/setup-lock-race-probe.ts. ADR 0001 amended with the mechanism only.
